tools.name: address_report
tools.description: One-call snapshot of any Base address: ETH balance, USDC balance, transaction count, and whether it is a smart contract or a regular wallet. Use it to sanity-check a counterparty or a payment address before sending funds. Input: a 0x address.

tools.name: token_info
tools.description: ERC-20 token metadata on Base, read on-chain: name, symbol, decimals, and total supply, plus whether the address really behaves like an ERC-20. Use it to verify a token contract before trusting or displaying it. Input: the token contract address (0x + 40 hex).

tools.name: token_balance
tools.description: How much of an ERC-20 token a wallet holds on Base, returned both human-formatted (using the token's decimals) and raw. Pass the token contract address and the holder address, both 0x + 40 hex. Example: USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913.

tools.name: gas_now
tools.description: Current gas price on the Base network (Coinbase's Ethereum L2), in gwei and wei, read live from a Base RPC node. Use before sending a Base transaction or estimating its cost. Takes no input.

tools.name: tx_status
tools.description: Look up a Base transaction by hash and report whether it is pending, succeeded, or failed, with from, to, value, block number, and gas used. Use it to confirm a payment or contract call landed. Input: the transaction hash (0x + 64 hex; the 0x is optional).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "address_report" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "One-call snapshot of a Base address: ETH balance, USDC balance, tx count, and whether it is a contract." → after: "One-call snapshot of any Base address: ETH balance, USDC balance, transaction count, and whether it is a smart contract or a regular wallet. Use it to sanity-check a counterparty or a payment address before sending funds. Input: a 0x address."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
